title: Four Months In, How's Your Will to Teach https://davestuartjr.com/four-months-in-hows-your-heart-plus-writing-intentions-for-back-to-school
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Marking exactly four months since Michigan's initial COVID school closures, Dave Stuart Jr. names the "carousel of mental maladies" — concern, overwhelm, anxiety, fear, anger, frustration, apathy — that many American educators were carrying as they faced an uncertain back-to-school season across remote, in-person, and hybrid scenarios. Rather than offering easy answers, he previews two threads he plans to pursue on the blog through the rest of the summer: sustaining "the will to teach" amid pandemic-era pressure, and adapting "the work that matters most" in teaching to a distance-learning context by synthesizing his own book with Hattie, Fisher, and Frey's Distance Learning Playbook. The short post functions as a table of contents for the larger series, framing the moment as difficult but not "unintelligible, unapproachable, unworkable."
points: Stuart frames the post's timing precisely — 120 days, "a third of a year" — since Michigan's school closures, grounding the emotional stock-take in a specific milestone rather than vague fatigue.

He identifies four distinct back-to-school scenarios (remote, in-person, hybrid, or undecided) that were simultaneously true for different educators at that moment, underscoring the uncertainty of the period.

The piece explicitly previews two forthcoming content threads — "the will to teach" (inner work) and "the work that matters most" adapted to distance learning (outer work) — that structure his subsequent posts that summer.
His closing reframe — unprecedented doesn't mean unintelligible, unapproachable, or unworkable — sets the tone of grounded resourcefulness that carries through the rest of the series.
quotes: It's been four months since the first day of school closures in Michigan. Four months: 120 days; a third of a year.
In all scenarios, your inner world may resemble a carousel of mental maladies.
I've got no silver bullet for these, but in the weeks to come I plan to share a few swords. We've for sure got bogeymen coming — internal and external — but we're not resourceless.
The will to teach — that's the fundamental inner wrestling match. With so much change and risk and pressure and toxicity and fear and outrage, my goodness, how do we maintain our will to do the work?
I wrote a book on the work that matters most in teaching, but distance learning was nowhere on my grid at that time. Now it needs to be.
Whether distance or in-person, we teach from who we are. No escaping it. So in the weeks to come, I'll work to be practical: what can we do to strengthen our internal selves, come what may?
